_meta: A small vector index in 2-D to show why approximate nearest-neighbor (ANN) search trades recall for speed. Exact nearest-neighbor search compares the query to every point (accurate but O(N)). An IVF (inverted-file) index instead partitions the points into clusters around centroids and, at query time, searches only the `nprobe` clusters nearest the query -- fast, because it skips most points, but it can MISS a true nearest neighbor that happens to sit in a cluster it did not search. That happens near cluster boundaries: a point just across the boundary from the query is one of the closest points overall, yet belongs to a different cluster than the query's own. query is the search vector; centroids define the clusters; points are the indexed vectors (each assigned to its nearest centroid); k is how many neighbors to return. Every distance, assignment, exact result, and IVF result is computed.
